atoms.text: This guide configures Tessera Loader, a batch ingestion service, to read raw CSV files from the bucket acme-raw-ingest and write Parquet output to the same bucket. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes. Create a role named tessera-loader-role and attach a trust policy that allows the Tessera Loader service to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows GetObject and ListBucket on the prefix incoming/ and PutObject on the prefix curated/. Do not modify the bucket policy of acme-raw-ingest; it stays exactly as it is. In the Tessera Loader job definition, set the execution role to tessera-loader-role so each run uses temporary credentials issued for that role. Run a test job that converts one sample file from incoming/ to curated/. Confirm in the access logs that the requests were made by the assumed-role session and that no write occurred outside curated/. If a request is denied, review the role's identity-based policy and its resource paths.

This guide configures Tessera Loader, a batch ingestion service, to read raw CSV files from the bucket acme-raw-ingest and write Parquet output to the same bucket. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the bucket policy of acme-raw-ingest whose principal is the service principal tessera-loader.service.example.com. The statement allows GetObject and ListBucket on the prefix incoming/ and PutObject on the prefix curated/. Leave the Tessera Loader job definition without an execution role, so each run authenticates as the service principal itself. Run a test job that converts one sample file from incoming/ to curated/. Confirm in the access logs that the requests were made by the service principal and that no write occurred outside curated/. If a request is denied, review the bucket policy statement and its resource paths.

This guide lets QuerySpan, an interactive SQL engine, scan web server logs in the bucket acme-weblogs and save query results to the bucket acme-query-results. Access is granted only through an IAM role that QuerySpan assumes. Create a role named queryspan-exec-role whose trust policy permits the QuerySpan service to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows GetObject and ListBucket on acme-weblogs, plus PutObject and GetBucketLocation on acme-query-results under the prefix results/. Do not edit the bucket policy of either bucket. In the QuerySpan workspace settings, set the query execution role to queryspan-exec-role and set the result location to results/. Run a SELECT statement against one day of logs and verify that a result file appears under results/. Check the audit trail to confirm the reads and writes are attributed to the assumed-role session. Any denial should be traced to the role's identity-based policy.

This guide lets QuerySpan, an interactive SQL engine, scan web server logs in the bucket acme-weblogs and save query results to the bucket acme-query-results. Access is granted only through the resource-based policies of the two buckets, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the policy of acme-weblogs naming the service principal queryspan.service.example.com, allowing GetObject and ListBucket. Add a statement to the policy of acme-query-results naming the same principal, allowing PutObject and GetBucketLocation under the prefix results/. In the QuerySpan workspace settings, leave the execution role empty and set the result location to results/. Run a SELECT statement against one day of logs and verify that a result file appears under results/. Check the audit trail to confirm the reads and writes are attributed to the service principal. Any denial should be traced to the bucket policy statements.

This guide gives Fluxmerge, a file compaction service, access to the bucket acme-events so it can read many small JSON files and write larger compacted files. Access is granted only through an IAM role that Fluxmerge assumes. Create a role named fluxmerge-compactor-role with a trust policy that allows the Fluxmerge service to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows ListBucket and GetObject on the prefix events/hourly/ and PutObject on the prefix events/compacted/. The bucket policy of acme-events must remain unchanged. Register the role in the Fluxmerge compaction schedule so that each hourly run requests temporary credentials for it. After the first run, list events/compacted/ and check that the number of output files is lower than the number of input files. Review the access logs to verify that every request came from the assumed-role session. If the run fails with an authorization error, correct the actions or resources in the role's policy.

This guide allows Ledgerline, a scheduled reporting service, to read nightly transaction exports from the bucket acme-finance-exports and write daily aggregate reports back under a separate prefix. Access is granted only through an IAM role that Ledgerline assumes. Create a role named ledgerline-report-role and set its trust policy so the Ledgerline service can assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows GetObject and ListBucket on the prefix exports/nightly/ and PutObject on the prefix reports/daily/. Do not change the bucket policy of acme-finance-exports. In the Ledgerline schedule definition, set the run-as role to ledgerline-report-role and the schedule to 02:00 UTC. Trigger a manual run for one date and confirm that a report object named with that date appears under reports/daily/. Inspect the access logs to verify that the read and write requests were issued by the assumed-role session. Permission errors are resolved by editing the role's identity-based policy.

This guide configures Auditrail Scan, a data validation service, to read newly landed files from the bucket acme-landing, write validation reports to one prefix, and copy rejected files to a quarantine prefix. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes. Create a role named auditrail-scan-role with a trust policy that lets the Auditrail Scan service assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows GetObject and ListBucket on landing/, and PutObject on both reports/ and quarantine/. The bucket policy of acme-landing is not modified. In the Auditrail Scan pipeline settings, specify auditrail-scan-role as the access role and enable scanning on new objects under landing/. Upload one valid file and one malformed file to landing/. Verify that a report appears under reports/ for both files and that only the malformed file is copied to quarantine/. Confirm in the access logs that all requests used assumed-role credentials.

This guide grants Featurewright, a feature extraction service, access to the bucket acme-clickstream so it can read raw session records and write feature snapshots. Access is granted only through an IAM role that Featurewright assumes. Create a role named featurewright-job-role and add a trust policy that allows the Featurewright service to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows ListBucket and GetObject on the prefix sessions/raw/ and PutObject on the prefix features/snapshots/. Leave the bucket policy of acme-clickstream untouched. In the Featurewright job configuration, set the role field to featurewright-job-role and the output path to features/snapshots/. Start a job over one hour of session data and wait for it to finish. Verify that snapshot files exist under features/snapshots/ and that the input prefix is unchanged. Use the access logs to confirm that requests were authenticated through the assumed role. A failed job with an access denied message points to the role's identity-based policy.

The statement allows ListBucket and GetObject on the prefix sessions/raw/ and PutObject on the prefix features/snapshots/. In the Featurewright job configuration, omit the role field and set the output path to features/snapshots/. Start a job over one hour of session data and wait for it to finish. Verify that snapshot files exist under features/snapshots/ and that the input prefix is unchanged. Use the access logs to confirm that requests were authenticated as the service principal. A failed job with an access denied message points to the bucket policy statement.

This guide sets up Beacon Ingest, a partner data intake service, to read files dropped in the bucket acme-partner-drop and write deduplicated copies to a processed prefix. Access is granted only through an IAM role that Beacon Ingest assumes. Create a role named beacon-ingest-role whose trust policy allows the Beacon Ingest service to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows GetObject, ListBucket and DeleteObject on the prefix drop/ and PutObject on the prefix processed/. The bucket policy of acme-partner-drop stays as it is. In the Beacon Ingest source configuration, enter beacon-ingest-role as the role to use for the bucket. Place two files with identical content in drop/ and wait for the next poll cycle, which runs every five minutes. Verify that processed/ contains a single copy and that drop/ no longer holds the originals. Check the access logs to confirm that the requests came from the assumed-role session.

Verify that processed/ contains a single copy and that drop/ no longer holds the originals. Check the access logs to confirm that the requests came from the service principal.

This guide enables Cinderpipe, a warehouse export service, to read extract files from the bucket acme-warehouse-staging and write date-partitioned snapshots to the same bucket. Access is granted only through an IAM role that Cinderpipe assumes. Create a role named cinderpipe-export-role and give it a trust policy that allows the Cinderpipe service to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows GetObject and ListBucket on the prefix extracts/ and PutObject on the prefix snapshots/. No change is made to the bucket policy of acme-warehouse-staging. In the Cinderpipe export definition, set the assumed role to cinderpipe-export-role and the partition scheme to snapshots/year=YYYY/month=MM/day=DD/. Run the export once and list the snapshots/ prefix to confirm that files were written under the expected partition path. Verify in the access logs that the requests were made with credentials issued for the role. Correct any authorization failure in the role's identity-based policy.
